note: Humanizer pass over RC527 (owner request 2026-11-02: 'humanizer manuscript'). Exact replacements for AI-writing patterns in the lore and a few prose lines; no rule, number, name, or bold term changes. Unapproved: the owner approves by patch ID before promotion, and the approved patches' status becomes 'approved'.

patches.find: The battlefield is never passive. Neutral Monsters stalk the field, hazards punish hesitation, and scenarios place pressure on both sides from the first activation to the last. Even victory is rarely clean. The party
patches.replace: Neutral Monsters stalk the field, hazards punish hesitation, and scenarios place pressure on both sides from the first activation to the last. The party
patches.note: The opener announces what the next sentence shows, and 'Even victory is rarely clean' restates the closing sentence. Both go; the three facts and the closing line stay.

patches.find: Merchants who travel between holdings are not soft clerks with ledgers. They bargain, lie, fight, navigate, and plan funerals with equal care. They know which inns change names too often. They know which milestones bleed in rain.
patches.replace: Merchants who travel between holdings bargain, lie, fight, navigate, and plan funerals with equal care. They know which inns change names too often and which milestones bleed in rain.
patches.note: Nobody claimed merchants were soft clerks; the list of what they do makes the point. The two 'They know which' sentences merge. RC523 polished the 'soft clerks' phrase, so decline this patch if you want to keep it.

patches.find: The dead do not always stay down. Some rise hungry. Some rise bitter. Some rise with orders still clenched behind their teeth.
patches.replace: The dead do not always stay down: some rise hungry, some bitter, and some with orders still clenched behind their teeth.
patches.note: Three fragments with the same opening become one sentence; all three kinds of dead stay.

patches.find: Coin waits there. Relics wait there. Forbidden lore waits there too, written in
patches.replace: Coin and relics wait there, and so does forbidden lore, written in
patches.note: 'X waits there' three times in a row.

patches.find: The lands where Heraldry Skirmish is fought are not a kingdom. They are a continent in the oldest sense:
patches.replace: The lands where Heraldry Skirmish is fought are a continent in the oldest sense:
patches.note: The negative half denies a claim nobody made; the rest of the sentence already says the crowns and borders stopped being useful.

patches.find: *The world is not dying gently. It dies like a wounded animal under a hedge. Slow. Aware. Dangerous to touch.*
patches.replace: *The world is dying the way a wounded animal dies under a hedge: slowly, aware of it, and dangerous to touch.*
patches.note: A 'not X, it is Y' opener followed by a row of one-word fragments. The image and all three qualities stay.

patches.find: *Beyond the walls, land has become allegiance. Expedition ledgers still say
patches.replace: *Expedition ledgers still say
patches.note: An aphorism with no claim the paragraph goes on to support; the paragraph is about names and labels.

patches.find: The forest is no wilderness. It is a country that does not recognize human law.*
patches.replace: The forest is a country of its own, and it does not recognize human law.*
patches.note: Split 'not X. It is Y.' closer stated directly.

patches.find: *These six are the world now. The Bastions are what mortal civilization built against them. They are also what mortal civilization hides inside.*
patches.replace: *The Bastions are what mortal civilization built against these six climates, and what it hides inside.*
patches.note: 'These six are the world now' restates the section; the two Bastion sentences share a subject and merge.

patches.find: They send envoys. They trade iron, salt, grain, oil, bodies, medicine, and lies. They exchange prisoners when it is useful. They accept refugees when plague at the gate would be worse than charity. Their treaties are thin things. Tired clerks write them. Hungry captains break them. No Bastion can afford open war with another. No Bastion trusts that fact to last.*
patches.replace: They send envoys and trade iron, salt, grain, oil, bodies, medicine, and lies. They exchange prisoners when it is useful and accept refugees when plague at the gate would be worse than charity. Their treaties are thin things, written by tired clerks and broken by hungry captains. No Bastion can afford open war with another, and none trusts that fact to last.*
patches.note: Nine short sentences, four opening 'They' and two 'No Bastion', become four. Every item stays.

patches.find: *The Bastions are not safe. They are safer. Their walls keep out the worst of the dark, not hunger,
patches.replace: *The Bastions are only safer than the country around them. Their walls keep out the worst of the dark, but not hunger,
patches.note: 'Not safe. They are safer.' is the staged form; the plain comparison says the same thing. 'but' repairs the list that follows.

patches.find: The **Town Phase** is not peace. It is the part of the war fought with ledgers, knives, prayers, and closed doors.*
patches.replace: The **Town Phase** is the part of the war fought with ledgers, knives, prayers, and closed doors.*
patches.note: 'Part of the war' already says it is not peace.

patches.find: It has the only reliable water for a hundred miles. This makes it wealthy. It also makes it hated.*
patches.replace: It has the only reliable water for a hundred miles, which makes it wealthy and hated.*
patches.note: Two follow-up fragments merge into the sentence they explain.

patches.find: Most Bastions tolerate wizards because they are useful. Tolerance is not trust. Sablekeep
patches.replace: Most Bastions tolerate wizards because they are useful. No Bastion trusts them. Sablekeep
patches.note: 'Tolerance is not trust' is an aphorism standing in for the plain claim.

patches.find: *The **Monsters** of the Dying Lands are not scattered obstacles. They hold the world now.
patches.replace: *The **Monsters** of the Dying Lands hold the world now.
patches.note: The negative half denies a claim nobody made. Chapter 9 opens with the same move (MON-01).

patches.find: Some bargain. Some tithe. Some raid. Some remember treaties
patches.replace: Some bargain, some tithe, and some raid. Some remember treaties
patches.note: Four 'Some' sentences in a row; the three one-word ones merge.

patches.find: *What works is a party of four. Small enough to hide. Strong enough to fight. Cheap enough to lose.*
patches.replace: *What works is a party of four: small enough to hide, strong enough to fight, and cheap enough to lose.*
patches.note: A row of fragments becomes one sentence; the three qualities stay. The same row appears again in Chapter 11 (CAMP-02). RC523 reworded 'Strong enough to fight'; that wording is kept.

patches.find: *Those who survive begin to build something larger than a purse. A keep on a hill. A reclaimed manor. A forge, a chapel, a vault, and a wall
patches.replace: *Those who survive begin to build something larger than a purse: a keep on a hill or a reclaimed manor, with a forge, a chapel, a vault, and a wall
patches.note: Three fragments become the end of the sentence they illustrate.

patches.find: A scenario does not need to explain the whole world. It needs only enough history
patches.replace: A scenario needs only enough history
patches.note: Split 'does not need X. It needs only Y.' stated directly.

patches.find: *Adventuring parties are not the heroes sung about in warm halls. They are the people
patches.replace: *Adventuring parties are the people
patches.note: Optional. The negative half does push against a genre expectation, so keep it if that is the point; the next sentences make the same point with specifics.

patches.find: *A Bastion blesses these parties when it must. It pays them when it can. It denies them when the work turns shameful.
patches.replace: *A Bastion blesses these parties when it must, pays them when it can, and denies them when the work turns shameful.
patches.note: Three parallel sentences become one.

patches.find: Stealth is not a flourish to them. It is the trade that buys supper.*
patches.replace: To them, stealth is the trade that buys supper.*
patches.note: 'Not a flourish. It is...' denies a claim nobody made.

patches.find: Speed was never a convenience. It was the difference between arriving and being found later.*
patches.replace: Speed was the difference between arriving and being found later.*
patches.note: Same move as PARTY-03.

patches.find: Coin is never only money to them. It is movement, influence, and another season behind the walls.*
patches.replace: To them, coin means movement, influence, and another season behind the walls.*
patches.note: 'Never only X. It is Y.' stated directly.

patches.find: You have found their crown. This is not the same thing, and the distinction matters, but perhaps not yet.*
patches.replace: You have found their crown, which is not the same as finding them. In time, the difference will matter.*
patches.note: 'The distinction matters' is the stock closer. The rewrite keeps the contrast, which here carries the point, and keeps the warning that it will matter later.

patches.find: *An iron-shod walking staff that has been struck against standing stones. Three times. The strikes are still there. Three dents in the iron cap,
patches.replace: *An iron-shod walking staff that has been struck three times against standing stones. The strikes are still there: three dents in the iron cap,
patches.note: A one-phrase fragment ('Three times.') folds into the sentence it belongs to.

patches.find: This is the staff. The dents are there. The iron cap is still warm.*
patches.replace: This is the staff, dents and all, and the iron cap is still warm.*
patches.note: Three fragments in a row.

patches.find: The stone counts everything now. It remembers every debt. It is very patient.*
patches.replace: The stone counts everything now and remembers every debt. It is very patient.*
patches.note: Optional. Merges two of the three closing fragments; the dry last line stays.

patches.find: Karnessa's Binding is the principle of that seal made portable. It is cold. It is always cold.*
patches.replace: Karnessa's Binding is the principle of that seal made portable, and it is always cold.*
patches.note: 'It is X. It is always X.' is used as the closer on several relics (also ITEM-06 and SCEN-01); this keeps the fact once.

patches.find: The Bell's Tongue has no provenance. It has always existed. It has always been cold.*
patches.replace: The Bell's Tongue has no provenance. It has always existed, and it has always been cold.*
patches.note: Same closer as ITEM-05; two fragments merge.

patches.find: It is always warm. Additionally, while you wear Kest's Iron Reliquary you may spend **[1 AP]**
patches.replace: It is always warm. While you wear Kest's Iron Reliquary, you may also spend **[1 AP]**
patches.note: Wording only; the effect is unchanged.

patches.find: Additionally, **Undead** and **Fiends** that attack you while you are within **2"** of such a threshold suffer **1d6 holy damage**
patches.replace: **Undead** and **Fiends** that attack you while you are within **2"** of such a threshold also suffer **1d6 holy damage**
patches.note: Wording only; the effect is unchanged.

patches.find: Additionally, while wearing this Seal, you gain **+1** on **SPI Checks**
patches.replace: While wearing this Seal, you also gain **+1** on **SPI Checks**
patches.note: Wording only; the effect is unchanged.

patches.find: **Effect:** This item functions as an early warning system. When any
patches.replace: **Effect:** This item is an early warning system. When any
patches.note: 'Functions as' where 'is' says the same thing. (The Monster abilities that 'function as' another ability keep that wording, because there it means 'use the rules of'.)

patches.find: until the end of the round. Additionally, you gain **+1** on **SPI Checks** made to resist **Frightened** from **Undead** sources.
patches.replace: until the end of the round. You also gain **+1** on **SPI Checks** made to resist **Frightened** from **Undead** sources.
patches.note: Wording only; the effect is unchanged.

patches.find: *In the Dying Lands, magic is not a gift; it is a symptom of a broken world. To cast a spell is to reach into the cracks of reality and pull something volatile through, a transaction that always leaves a stain. The common folk know better than to trust it, having learned to fear its touch through generations of curses, twisted omens, and localized catastrophe. Sensible people cling to the safety of timber walls and the comforting heft of cold iron. But the desperate, the greedy, and the doomed recognize that surviving the ruins often requires bargaining with forces that transcend the swing of a blade.*
patches.replace: *In the Dying Lands, magic is a symptom of a broken world. To cast a spell is to reach into the cracks of reality and pull something volatile through, and the transaction always leaves a stain. Generations of curses, twisted omens, and local catastrophes have taught the common folk to fear its touch. Sensible people keep to timber walls and cold iron. The desperate, the greedy, and the doomed know that surviving the ruins often means bargaining with forces no blade can reach.*
patches.note: The Chapter 8 introduction is the most machine-sounding passage in the book. This paragraph drops the 'not a gift' contrast, 'transcend', 'the comforting heft of', and the participle chain, and keeps every claim.

patches.find: each scarred, perilous, and profoundly changed.*
patches.replace: each scarred, perilous, and much changed.*
patches.note: 'Profoundly' is decoration.

patches.find: *Arcane Spells are the hollow inheritance of the old world. Wizards are less miracle-workers than they are magical scavengers, piecing together forbidden principles from half-burned grimoires and the silent, dust-choked observatories where their predecessors still sit slumped in death. Their craft is a cold calculus of arcane formulae and unstable geometry. While Bastions tolerate them for their sheer utility, wizards are rarely loved, and are invariably blamed the moment a working leaks or the dead begin to walk.*
patches.replace: *Arcane Spells are the hollow inheritance of the old world. Wizards are scavengers, piecing together forbidden principles from half-burned grimoires and from silent, dust-choked observatories where their predecessors still sit slumped in death. Their craft runs on arcane formulae and unstable geometry. The Bastions tolerate wizards because they are useful, rarely love them, and blame them the moment a working leaks or the dead begin to walk.*
patches.note: Drops 'less X than they are Y', 'cold calculus', 'sheer utility', and 'invariably'. Same claims, plainer verbs.

patches.find: *Divine Prayers are whispered into a largely empty sky. The old saints remain in the chapel rolls, but they answer fitfully, if they answer at all. A priest capable of calling down a true working is a rarity, famous enough to command reverence and terrifying enough to be feared. The faithful fracture over the silence: some preach that the gods retreated in disgust at an unnameable insult, while others insist mortal souls simply lack the worthiness to be heard. Regardless of the doctrine, divine magic is a desperate plea for a miracle, fuelled by fanatical devotion and answered only in blood and light.*
patches.replace: *Divine Prayers are whispered into a largely empty sky. The old saints remain in the chapel rolls, but they answer fitfully, if at all. A priest who can call down a true working is rare, revered, and feared. The faithful split over the silence: some preach that the gods withdrew in disgust at an insult no scripture will name, and others that mortal souls are not yet worthy to be heard. Whatever the doctrine, a prayer is a desperate plea for a miracle, fuelled by fanatical devotion and answered only in blood and light.*
patches.note: Plainer wording. 'An insult no scripture will name' and 'not yet worthy' match the wording 1.3.1 and 1.3.4 already use for the same two doctrines.

patches.find: *Druidic Rituals pulse with a terrifying, untamed vitality. Unlike the crumbling arcane or the silent divine, the magic of the wild has only grown more ferocious since the Fall. Druids commune with the encroaching forests, the choking bogs, and the violent storms. Their oldest circles do not mourn the dying world; instead, they teach that the earth is merely shedding mortal civilization like dead skin, and they act as the ruthless midwives to this violent rebirth.*
patches.replace: *Druidic Rituals draw on the wild, and while arcane learning crumbles and the gods stay silent, the wild has only grown more ferocious since the Fall. Druids commune with the encroaching forests, the choking bogs, and the violent storms. Their oldest circles do not mourn the dying world. They teach that the earth is shedding mortal civilization like dead skin, and they attend that violent rebirth like ruthless midwives.*
patches.note: Drops 'pulse with a terrifying, untamed vitality' and 'act as'. The 'do not mourn' contrast stays, because it marks the difference from the other traditions.

patches.find: *Sorceries represent the most volatile and treacherous path to power, demanding a terrible intimacy with corruption. Some sorcerers are twisted by exposure to blighted ruin-sites, while others suffer from ancestral wounds reopening generations later, or strike infernal pacts in their darkest, most desperate hours. They wield raw, unrefined destruction, paying for their output in their own blood. Hanged in the streets of Sablekeep and treated with extreme caution everywhere else, sorcerers are living conduits of the world's sickness.*
patches.replace: *Sorceries are the most volatile and treacherous path to power, and the closest to corruption. Some sorcerers are twisted by exposure to blighted ruin-sites. Others carry ancestral wounds that reopen generations later, or strike infernal pacts in their most desperate hours. They wield raw destruction and pay for it in their own blood. Sablekeep hangs them in the streets, and everywhere else treats them with extreme caution. The world's sickness runs through every one of them.*
patches.note: 'Represent' becomes 'are'; drops 'terrible intimacy', 'raw, unrefined', 'paying for their output', and 'living conduits'.

patches.find: *Psychic Abilities remain the rarest, strangest, and least understood of the traditions. Psions do not study their power; they survive it. Their minds are cracked open by the long, suffocating pressure of sunken crypts, exposure to thought-eater nests, or sheer proximity to the alien things sleeping beneath the Undermarches. They emerge from the dark hearing the jagged thoughts of everyone around them. They are rarely hunted with the same religious fervour as sorcerers, but they are never trusted, for no one welcomes a person who can weaponize a memory or peel back the privacy of a skull.*
patches.replace: *Psychic Abilities remain the rarest and least understood of the traditions. A psion's mind is cracked open by the long, suffocating pressure of sunken crypts, by exposure to thought-eater nests, or by nearness to the alien things sleeping beneath the Undermarches, and it comes out of the dark hearing the jagged thoughts of everyone nearby. Psions are rarely hunted with the religious fervour reserved for sorcerers, but they are never trusted, because no one welcomes a person who can weaponize a memory or peel back the privacy of a skull.*
patches.note: Drops the 'do not study; they survive' contrast (the Psion class text already says 'not so much chosen as survived') and the padded triad.

patches.find: *At this height a prayer is not asked but demanded, and something always answers.
patches.replace: *At this height a prayer is a demand, and something always answers.
patches.note: 'Not asked but demanded' stated directly.

patches.find: *Sorcery does not study. It bleeds. These first workings
patches.replace: *Sorcery is learned by bleeding. These first workings

patches.find: The creatures encountered in the Dying Lands are not interruptions to an expedition; they are the present owners of the world.
patches.replace: The creatures encountered in the Dying Lands are the present owners of the world.
patches.note: Same move as LORE-15.

patches.find: To enter the wilds is not to wander into empty land. It is to trespass.*
patches.replace: To enter the wilds is to trespass.*

patches.find: One wererat is a nuisance; a nest of them is an outbreak.*
patches.replace: A nest of them is an outbreak.*

patches.find: One alone is nothing; a chittering mob of them,
patches.replace: A chittering mob of them,
patches.note: See MON-03.

patches.replace: They melt into the cover and strike from wherever the water hides them, and in a swarm they are dangerous. They strip

patches.replace: The Mire's dusk air hums with them, and a swarm can drain a body dry.*

patches.find: they will hold that post when the last warm thing in the world goes out. There are always more under the snow.*

patches.replace: They draw a trail of cinders across the tomb-floors.*

patches.find: The court's justice did not die with the court. It only grew patient.*
patches.replace: The court's justice outlived the court and only grew patient.*

patches.find: Their breath does not merely freeze; it stops time in the flesh,

patches.find: Their breath neither burns nor freezes but unmakes, peeling away
patches.replace: Their breath unmakes, peeling away

patches.find: They no longer recall the war they are still fighting. Only the oath.*
patches.replace: They no longer recall the war they are still fighting, only the oath.*
patches.note: A one-phrase fragment joins its sentence.

patches.find: They do not speak. They do not negotiate. They maintain the terms.*
